title: Peel this page back to read the HTML the server sent
blurb: The whole page is drawn by one canvas. Drag its top right corner and the page rolls back like paper. Under it is the HTML of this page as the server streamed it, and nothing else.
question: Can a canvas draw a whole scrolling page, roll it back from a corner under a finger, and hand input to a layer of source text under it along the roll?
result: Yes in Chromium 157. The page is a scrolling box inside one screen-sized canvas. A shader rolls it back and leaves clear pixels, and a clip-path on the canvas host, computed from the same numbers, sends taps and scrolling beyond the roll to the source text under it. The frame rate on a phone isn't verified: the page reports it.
